title: Outlook for iOS and iPad: work week calendar view
summary: Hold: the briefing makes unsupported assurances that the view introduces no new data access, permissions or sharing paths. The roadmap details, release build, app licensing and absence of a documented view-specific admin switch are supported, but Microsoft does not establish those broader assurances.

claims.where: What's changing: synced days; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not explain which default-account setting supplies the mobile work week days or precedence between synced and device-specific days.
claims.quote: Searched: "work week" "iOS" "default account"; Outlook iOS work week view default account sync working days data access sharing permissions. Read release notes, FAQ, app configuration and Graph workingHours excerpts; none connects mobile work week to a setting or states precedence.

claims.where: Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The roadmap and release notes describe no change to users' existing calendar views.
claims.quote: Searched: "Outlook" "work week" "iOS" "permissions" "default". Read roadmap description and release notes work week entry; both describe choosing the view, neither states that existing selected views are changed.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The view reads nothing new and reaches only the user's existing calendar data.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS work week view default account sync working days data access sharing permissions. Opened release notes, Outlook mobile FAQ and app configuration reference; the view entry does not specify its data-access boundary.
claims.fix: Remove 'It shows the user's own calendar over fewer days, so it opens no new data, permission or sharing path.' Replace the Data exposure bullet with 'Microsoft describes a calendar view focused on work days; its release notes do not describe additional data access.' Replace 'it shows the same calendar data and reaches nothing new' in the risk rationale with 'Microsoft describes it as a calendar view focused on work days'.

claims.fix: Remove 'It shows the user's own calendar over fewer days, so it opens no new data, permission or sharing path.' Retain the narrower Security & identity statement that Microsoft describes no new permission for the view.
